title: Two views of the grinding stones at Hovra
bodyMd:
**Text 1**

At the site of Hovra, archaeologist Petter Lund recovered grinding stones from a soil layer dated to about 9,000 years ago. Starch granules from wild barley cling to the stones' surfaces. Lund concludes that people at Hovra were grinding wild grain at least 9,000 years ago, several centuries before the earliest evidence of farming in the region.

**Text 2**

Archaeological chemist Amara Osei has shown that starch granules can be carried downward through soil by water, so starch found on a tool may be much younger than the layer in which the tool lies. Starch sealed deep inside the tiny cracks of a grinding surface, by contrast, stays in place. Osei notes that Lund's published report does not say whether any of his samples came from such cracks.
